title: Expert Witness Report — Cause No. 2025-CV-03821
text:
EXPERT WITNESS REPORT OF DR. ELENA M. O’NEIL

I, Dr. Elena M. O’Neil, being duly sworn, depose and state as follows:

1. I am a board-certified forensic engineer with over twenty years of experience in structural failure analysis. I have been retained by counsel for the plaintiff, Bryant Law Firm, on behalf of Ms. Deborah Bryant, to render an opinion regarding the collapse of a retaining wall at 1427 Pecan Grove Lane, Austin, Travis County, Texas.

2. My qualifications are set forth in my curriculum vitae, attached hereto as Exhibit A. I have previously testified in state and federal courts, including in Texas, California, and New York.

3. The opposing party is Greenfield Construction, LLC, represented by its counsel, Mr. Richard J. Holloway of Holloway & Associates. The presiding judge is the Honorable Maria T. Vasquez of the 353rd Judicial District Court.

4. The incident occurred on March 12, 2024, when the retaining wall on Ms. Bryant’s property gave way during heavy rainfall, causing significant damage to her home and personal property. Ms. Bryant’s date of birth is November 4, 1971.

5. I inspected the site on April 2, 2024, and reviewed the following documents: (a) the construction contract between Ms. Bryant and Greenfield Construction, dated January 15, 2023; (b) engineering drawings prepared by Hartfield Engineering, Inc.; (c) daily work logs; and (d) photographs of the site. The documents produced by defendant bear Bates range BRYANT0001–BRYANT0450.

6. In my opinion, the wall failed because the drainage system was improperly installed. The design called for a perforated pipe behind the wall, but the as-built condition shows no such pipe. As noted in the deposition of Mr. Thomas Hartfield, P.E., “the design was clear, but [Hartfield] did not supervise installation.”

7. This case involves a vehicle owned by Ms. Bryant, a 2021 Ford F-150 with VIN 1FTFW1E53MFA12345, which was damaged by falling debris. Her insurance policy number is TX-87654321-00, issued by Lone Star Mutual Insurance.

8. Relevant legal authority: The duty of a contractor to perform in a workmanlike manner is established under Texas law. See Melody Home Mfg. Co. v. Barnes, 741 S.W.2d 349 (Tex. 1987); see also Humber v. O’Malley, 669 S.W.2d 754 (Tex. App.—Houston [1st Dist.] 1984, writ ref’d n.r.e.). Additionally, the Texas Residential Construction Liability Act, Tex. Prop. Code § 27.001 et seq., governs claims arising from construction defects.

9. I have also considered the deposition testimony of Mr. exhibitJohn Doe, a former employee of Greenfield Construction, who stated that he observed shortcuts during the wall’s construction.

10. My bar number is 24098765. I may be reached at (512) 555-0198 or by email at e.oneil@forensiceng.com.

I declare under penalty of perjury that the foregoing is true and correct.

Executed this 15th day of October, 2025.

/s/ Dr. Elena M. O’Neil

Cause No. 2025-CV-03821; Deborah Bryant v. Greenfield Construction, LLC

title: Expert Witness Report — Cause No. 2025-CV-04112
text:
EXPERT WITNESS REPORT OF MR. JAMES P. HARRIS

I, James P. Harris, P.E., am a licensed professional engineer in the State of Texas, bar number 87654321. I submit this report in connection with the above-captioned matter.

1. I was retained by counsel for the plaintiff, the Law Offices of Thompson & Reed, on behalf of Mr. Carlos M. Reyes, to evaluate the cause of a fire at 8902 Elm Street, Dallas, Dallas County, Texas.

2. The opposing party is FireSafe Manufacturing Corp., represented by its counsel, Ms. Jessica L. Kim of Kim & Partners. The case is assigned to Judge Samuel R. Whitfield of the 191st Judicial District Court.

3. Mr. Reyes’s date of birth is March 22, 1985. His Social Security number is 456-78-9012.

4. The fire occurred on July 19, 2024. I visited the scene on July 25, 2024. My investigation included review of the fire department report, witness statements, and the product in question — a Model FS-2000 space heater manufactured by FireSafe. The product’s policy number under FireSafe’s liability coverage is PL-99887766.

5. I also reviewed the deposition of Mr. Marcus T. Holloway, a former quality control inspector. During his deposition, he stated, “I told management about the faulty wiring, but [Holloway] was ignored.” The relevant documents were produced under Bates range REYES0001–REYES0320.

6. The fire originated in the living room, near the space heater. The heater’s serial number is FS-2000-8847. The home also had a vehicle in the driveway, a 2020 Toyota Camry with VIN 4T1B11HK7LU123456.

7. Legal standards: In Texas, a product liability claim for design defect is governed by the Texas Products Liability Act, Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 82.001 et seq. See also Caterpillar, Inc. v. Shears, 911 S.W.2d 379 (Tex. 1995); and Firestone Steel Products Co. v. Barajas, 927 S.W.2d 608 (Tex. 1996). The plaintiff bears the burden of proving that the product was unreasonably dangerous.

8. I have prepared a detailed analysis, attached as Exhibit B. My email is james.harris@engtest.com and my phone is (214) 555-0341.

I affirm that the facts herein are true and correct.

/s/ James P. Harris

Cause No. 2025-CV-04112; Carlos M. Reyes v. FireSafe Manufacturing Corp.
public_law: Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 82.001 et seq.
cited_case_parties: Firestone Steel Products Co. v. Barajas

title: Expert Witness Report — Cause No. 2025-CV-04298
text:
EXPERT WITNESS REPORT OF DR. LINDA S. PARKER

I, Dr. Linda S. Parker, M.D., am a board-certified neurologist. I am submitting this report in the matter of Patricia A. Jennings v. St. Luke’s Medical Center.

1. I was retained by the Law Firm of O’Connor & Mason, counsel for the plaintiff, Ms. Patricia A. Jennings. The defendant is St. Luke’s Medical Center, represented by its attorney, Mr. David K. Chen of Chen Legal Group. The case is before Judge Angela R. Moreno of the 215th Judicial District Court, Harris County.

2. Ms. Jennings’s date of birth is June 15, 1982. Her Social Security number is 123-45-6789. She was admitted to St. Luke’s on August 10, 2024, for a routine surgical procedure.

3. During the surgery, the patient suffered a hypoxic brain injury due to an anesthesia error. I have reviewed the anesthesia records, nursing notes, and the deposition of the anesthesiologist, Dr. exhibitJohn Smith. In his deposition, Dr. Smith stated: “The monitoring equipment was functioning, but [Smith] did not notice the drop in oxygen saturation.”

4. The medical records produced bear Bates range JENNINGS0001–JENNINGS0789. Ms. Jennings’s insurance policy number is HLTH-456123-89, from Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas.

5. The hospital’s own policy number for its malpractice coverage is MP-77889900, issued by Texas Medical Liability Trust.

6. I also note that Ms. Jennings drives a 2023 Honda Accord, VIN 1HGCV1F31PA012345.

7. Legal standards: The standard of care for anesthesiologists in Texas is well established. See Hood v. Phillips, 554 S.W.2d 160 (Tex. 1977); and see also Denton v. Yazoo Mfg. Co., 720 S.W.2d 678 (Tex. App.—El Paso 1986, writ ref’d n.r.e.). The Texas Medical Liability Act, Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 74.001 et seq., sets forth the requirements for medical malpractice claims.

8. I may be reached at (713) 555-0212 or l.s.parker@neuromd.com. My bar number is 76543210.

I declare under penalty of perjury that the foregoing is true.

/s/ Dr. Linda S. Parker

Cause No. 2025-CV-04298; Patricia A. Jennings v. St. Luke’s Medical Center

title: Expert Witness Report — Cause No. 2025-CV-04355
text:
EXPERT WITNESS REPORT OF DR. WILLIAM T. GRANT

I, Dr. William T. Grant, Ph.D., am a forensic accountant. I have been retained by the law firm of Bryant Law Firm on behalf of Ms. Deborah Bryant in the matter of Deborah Bryant v. Greenfield Construction, LLC (same as Cause No. 2025-CV-03821, but now for damages phase).

1. I was engaged to calculate economic damages resulting from the retaining wall collapse. My analysis includes loss of property value, temporary housing costs, and loss of use of the vehicle, a 2021 Ford F-150 with VIN 1FTFW1E53MFA12345.

2. The plaintiff is Ms. Deborah Bryant. The defendant is Greenfield Construction, LLC, represented by Mr. Richard J. Holloway. The case is before Judge Maria T. Vasquez.

3. Ms. Bryant’s date of birth is November 4, 1971. Her Social Security number is 987-65-4321.

4. I have reviewed the following: insurance claim files from Lone Star Mutual Insurance, policy number TX-87654321-00; bank statements from First Texas Bank; and the contract signed by Ms. Bryant and Mr. Thomas Hartfield of Hartfield Engineering.

5. The documents produced by plaintiff bear Bates range BRYANT0451–BRYANT0800. The defendant’s production is under Bates range GREEN0001–GREEN0200.

6. In the deposition of Mr. exhibitJohn Doe, he stated: “I saw the work was shoddy, but [Doe] was told to keep quiet.”

7. Legal authority: Damages recoverable for breach of contract in Texas include the benefit of the bargain. See Mays v. Pierce, 281 S.W.3d 461 (Tex. App.—El Paso 2006, pet. denied). See also Mustang Pipeline Co. v. Driver Pipeline Co., 134 S.W.3d 195 (Tex. 2004). The Texas Property Code § 27.004 provides for pre-suit notice requirements.

8. My bar number is 11223344. I can be contacted at (512) 555-0789 or w.grant@forensicacc.com.

I swear that the contents of this report are accurate.

/s/ Dr. William T. Grant

Cause No. 2025-CV-04355 (consolidated with 2025-CV-03821); Deborah Bryant v. Greenfield Construction, LLC
cited_case_parties: Mustang Pipeline Co. v. Driver Pipeline Co.

title: Expert Witness Report — Cause No. 2025-CV-04488
text:
EXPERT WITNESS REPORT OF MR. ANTHONY R. MORENO

I, Anthony R. Moreno, P.E., am a civil engineer. I submit this report in the case of Evelyn M. Chen-Whitfield v. Trinity River Development, Inc.

1. I was retained by the plaintiff’s counsel, the Law Office of Sarah J. O’Neil, P.C., on behalf of Ms. Evelyn M. Chen-Whitfield. The defendant is Trinity River Development, Inc., represented by its counsel, Mr. Mark A. Thompson of Thompson & Garcia. The case is assigned to Judge Leonard P. Durham of the 95th Judicial District Court, Dallas County.

2. Ms. Chen-Whitfield’s date of birth is September 12, 1978. Her Social Security number is 321-54-9876. She owns a 2022 Chevrolet Silverado with VIN 1GC1KVEY7NZ123456.

3. The dispute involves structural defects in a residential foundation at 4500 Arbor Lane, Dallas, Texas. The home was built by Trinity River Development. I inspected the property on October 5, 2024.

4. My review includes the geotechnical report by GeoTest Labs, Inc.; the construction contract; and the deposition of the site supervisor, Mr. exhibitJohn Peterson. In his testimony, Mr. Peterson said: “I flagged the soil issue, but [Peterson] was overruled.”

5. The documents produced by plaintiff bear Bates range CHEN0001–CHEN0600. The defendant’s production bears range TRINITY0001–TRINITY0400.

6. Ms. Chen-Whitfield’s homeowner’s insurance policy number is HO-334455-77, issued by Statewide Casualty Insurance.

7. Legal standards: The Texas Residential Construction Liability Act, Tex. Prop. Code § 27.001 et seq., governs this claim. See also Luker v. Arnold, 843 S.W.2d 719 (Tex. App.—Fort Worth 1992, no writ); and Walker v. Harris, 924 S.W.2d 375 (Tex. 1996).

8. I may be reached at (214) 555-0678 or a.moreno@structeng.com. My bar number is 99887766.

I certify under penalty of perjury that this report is true and correct.

/s/ Anthony R. Moreno

Cause No. 2025-CV-04488; Evelyn M. Chen-Whitfield v. Trinity River Development, Inc.
